# Village dock

Asset: `village-dock-pixel-v1.png`
Generated with the built-in `image_gen` tool on 2026-09-15. Original PNG and alpha retained. The shared village renderer uses it in scenes 1 and 8, with nearest-neighbor filtering. A small visual overhang accommodates the posts and transparent padding while the existing 6 × 2 walkable tile footprint stays the same.

Final prompt:

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: a single complete wooden fishing-village dock sprite for a 16-bit top-down Japanese RPG. Create one wide rectangular dock platform, width three times its height, intended to cover exactly 6 by 2 game tiles at 288x96 pixels. Strict overhead RPG view with only a tiny visible dark lower front rim. Crisp deliberate pixel art, approximately 192x64 logical pixels enlarged nearest-neighbor, no smooth antialiasing. Weathered warm honey-brown wooden planks running vertically from the shore-facing top to the sea-facing bottom; varied board lengths, subtle dark grain and knots, narrow charcoal-brown seams, small square iron nail heads, restrained sand-gold top-left highlights. Dark stout timber rim on left, right, bottom; four short square mooring posts close to the corners with a few simple rope pixels. Top edge remains an OPEN walkable entry from land, no railing across it. ONE cohesive pier, no repeating green tile bands, no green paint, no grass. Palette and tactile handcrafted detail should harmonize with richly textured pixel-art golden beach sand, cobalt water and a timber fishing village. Wide 3:1 image composition, dock fills almost all canvas with minimal transparent padding. Genuine transparent alpha outside the dock, no ocean, no water baked into sprite, no shore, no boats, no characters, no text, no background scene, no isometric diagonal perspective, no vector shapes, no photorealism.
